# openmetadata_policy (Data Source)

Looks up a single OpenMetadata policy by id or fully qualified name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openmetadata_policy" "viewer" {
  fully_qualified_name = "viewer"
}

output "viewer_policy_id" {
  value = data.openmetadata_policy.viewer.id
}

output "viewer_policy_rules" {
  value = data.openmetadata_policy.viewer.rules
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Policy fully qualified name. Exactly one of id or fully_qualified_name must be set.
- `id` (String) Policy UUID. Exactly one of id or fully_qualified_name must be set.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Markdown description.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy is active.
- `name` (String) Policy name.
- `rules` (Attributes Set) Rules granted by the policy. OpenMetadata sorts rules and operations itself, so this is a set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `condition` (String) Condition expression that narrows when the rule applies.
- `description` (String) Description of the rule.
- `effect` (String) Whether the rule allows or denies the operations.
- `name` (String) Rule name.
- `operations` (Set of String) Operations covered by the rule.
- `resources` (Set of String) Entity types the rule applies to.
